concepts.title: Unrolled Computation Graph
concepts.one_liner: An unrolled computation graph is a directed acyclic graph representation of a recurrent neural network over a finite number of timesteps.
concepts.content:
(see figure: RNN with multidimensional inputs, hidden states, and outputs.)

To the left is the unrolled computation graph. To the right is the computation graph rolled up, with a feedback connection. Typically we work with unrolled graphs because they are directed acyclic graphs (DAGs), and therefore all the tools developed for DAGs, including backpropagation, extend naturally to them. However, note that RNNs can run for unbounded time and process signals that have unbounded temporal extent, while a DAG can only represent a finite graph. The DAG depicted above is therefore a truncated version of the RNN's theoretical computation graph.
concepts.motivation_md: Standard backpropagation requires a directed acyclic graph (DAG). Since recurrent networks contain feedback loops, they must be "unrolled" into a DAG over a finite sequence of steps to allow for gradient-based optimization.
concepts.recap_md: - Unrolling transforms a recurrent network with feedback into a directed acyclic graph (DAG).

concepts.title: Recurrent Layer Definition
concepts.one_liner: A recurrent layer uses a state variable to produce outputs and update its own memory based on sequential inputs.
concepts.motivation_md: Standard feedforward layers process inputs independently. Recurrent layers introduce a state variable (memory) to allow the network to process sequential data where the current output depends on previous inputs.
concepts.recap_md: - Recurrent layers maintain a state $\mathbf{h}$ that acts as memory.

slots.motivation: Standard feedforward layers process inputs independently. Recurrent layers introduce a state variable (memory) to allow the network to process sequential data where the current output depends on previous inputs.
slots.key_passage: - Recurrent layers maintain a state $\mathbf{h}$ that acts as memory.

concepts.title: Sequential Computation and Time Indexing
concepts.one_liner: Time in an RNN refers to sequential computation where the timestep $t$ serves as an index into a sequence.
concepts.content: The idea of "time" in an RNN does not necessarily mean time as it is measured on a clock. Time just refers to sequential computation; the timestep $t$ is an index into the sequence. The sequential computation could progress over a spatial dimension (processing an image pixel by pixel), over the temporal dimension (processing a video frame by frame), or even over more abstracted computational modules.
concepts.motivation_md: RNNs are often associated with temporal data, but their architecture is applicable to any data that can be ordered sequentially, such as pixels in an image or tokens in a sentence.
concepts.recap_md: - Timestep $t$ is an index for sequential computation, not necessarily physical time.

slots.motivation: RNNs are often associated with temporal data, but their architecture is applicable to any data that can be ordered sequentially, such as pixels in an image or tokens in a sentence.

concepts.title: Simple Recurrent Network (SRN)
concepts.one_liner: The Simple Recurrent Network (SRN) is a recurrent layer where state updates and outputs are computed via linear layers and pointwise nonlinearities.
concepts.content:
One common kind of recurrent layer is the Simple Recurrent Network (SRN), defined by Elman in "Finding Structure in Time" (1990). For this layer, $f$ is a linear layer followed by a pointwise nonlinearity, and $g$ is another linear layer. The full computation is defined by the following equations: 
$$\begin{aligned}
    \mathbf{h}_t &= \sigma_1(\mathbf{W}\mathbf{h}_{t-1} + \mathbf{U}\mathbf{x}_{\texttt{in}}[t]+ \mathbf{b})\\
    \mathbf{x}_{\texttt{out}}[t]&= \sigma_2(\mathbf{V}\mathbf{h}_t + \mathbf{c})
\end{aligned}$$
where $\sigma_1$ and $\sigma_2$ are pointwise nonlinearities. In SRNs, tanh is the common choice for the nonlinearity, but ReLUs and other choices may also be used.
concepts.motivation_md: The SRN provides a basic architectural template for recurrence, using standard linear transformations and nonlinearities to maintain and update a hidden state over time.
concepts.recap_md: - SRNs update hidden states using a linear combination of the previous state and current input.

slots.motivation: The SRN provides a basic architectural template for recurrence, using standard linear transformations and nonlinearities to maintain and update a hidden state over time.
slots.key_passage: - SRNs update hidden states using a linear combination of the previous state and current input.

concepts.title: Backpropagation through Time (BPTT)
concepts.one_liner: Backpropagation through Time (BPTT) is the application of backpropagation to a recurrent neural network unrolled for a finite number of timesteps.
concepts.content:
Backpropagation is only defined for DAGs, and RNNs are not DAGs. To apply backpropagation to RNNs, we unroll the net for $T$ timesteps, which creates a DAG representation of the truncated RNN, and then do backpropagation through that DAG. This is known as Backpropagation through Time (BPTT).

This approach yields exact gradients of the loss with respect to the parameters when $T$ is equal to the total number of timesteps the RNN was run for. Otherwise, BPTT is an approximation that truncates the true computation graph. Essentially, BPTT ignores any dependencies in the computation graph greater than length $T$.
concepts.motivation_md: Since RNNs contain cycles, standard backpropagation cannot be applied directly. BPTT solves this by treating the unrolled sequence as a deep feedforward network where weights are shared across layers.
concepts.recap_md: - BPTT unrolls an RNN into a DAG for $T$ timesteps to enable gradient calculation.

slots.motivation: Since RNNs contain cycles, standard backpropagation cannot be applied directly. BPTT solves this by treating the unrolled sequence as a deep feedforward network where weights are shared across layers.
slots.key_passage: - BPTT unrolls an RNN into a DAG for $T$ timesteps to enable gradient calculation.

concepts.title: The Problem of Exploding and Vanishing Gradients
concepts.one_liner: Long sequences in RNNs can lead to gradients that either explode or vanish due to repeated matrix multiplications during backpropagation.
concepts.motivation_md: Training RNNs on long sequences is difficult because the chain rule results in repeated multiplications. This causes gradients to grow or shrink exponentially, preventing the network from learning long-term dependencies.
concepts.recap_md: - Gradients in RNNs involve a product of matrices proportional to the sequence length $T$.

slots.motivation: Training RNNs on long sequences is difficult because the chain rule results in repeated multiplications. This causes gradients to grow or shrink exponentially, preventing the network from learning long-term dependencies.
slots.key_passage: - Gradients in RNNs involve a product of matrices proportional to the sequence length $T$.

concepts.title: Long Short-Term Memory
concepts.one_liner: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks are specialized recurrent modules designed to mitigate vanishing and exploding gradients using a persistent cell state.
concepts.content:
Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs) are a special kind of recurrent module designed to avoid the vanishing and exploding gradients problem. An LSTM acts as a memory controller with a cell state, $\mathbf{c}$, which is a vector it can read from and write to. While both the cell state and the hidden state $\mathbf{h}$ record memories, the cell state is specifically built to store persistent memories that can last a long time.

Like a normal recurrent layer, an LSTM takes a hidden state $\mathbf{h}_{t-1}$ and an observation $\mathbf{x}_{\texttt{in}}[t]$ to produce an updated hidden state $\mathbf{h}_t$. Internally, the LSTM uses its cell state to decide how to update $\mathbf{h}_{t-1}$. Subcomponents of the LSTM layer determine what to delete from, write to, and read off the cell state to produce the final output.
concepts.motivation_md: Standard RNNs struggle to retain information over many timesteps due to numerical instability. LSTMs introduce a "gated" architecture that allows information to flow through a cell state with minimal interference, preserving long-term dependencies.
concepts.recap_md: - LSTMs use a cell state $\mathbf{c}$ to maintain persistent, long-term memory.

slots.motivation: Standard RNNs struggle to retain information over many timesteps due to numerical instability. LSTMs introduce a "gated" architecture that allows information to flow through a cell state with minimal interference, preserving long-term dependencies.
slots.key_passage: - LSTMs use a cell state $\mathbf{c}$ to maintain persistent, long-term memory.

concepts.title: LSTM Cell State
concepts.one_liner: The LSTM cell state is a vector designed to store persistent memories that can be read from or written to over long sequences.
concepts.content: An LSTM functions as a memory controller using a cell state, $\mathbf{c}$, which is a vector it can read from and write to. The cell state can record memories and retrieve them as needed. While it plays a similar role to the hidden state $\mathbf{h}$ in regular RNNs, the cell state is specifically designed to store persistent memories that can last for a long duration, giving the architecture its name: long short-term memory.
concepts.motivation_md: In standard RNNs, the hidden state is transformed at every step, making it hard to keep information unchanged. The cell state provides a dedicated pathway for information to persist across many steps without being overwritten.
concepts.recap_md: - The cell state $\mathbf{c}$ allows for the storage and retrieval of persistent memories.

slots.motivation: In standard RNNs, the hidden state is transformed at every step, making it hard to keep information unchanged. The cell state provides a dedicated pathway for information to persist across many steps without being overwritten.
slots.key_passage: - The cell state $\mathbf{c}$ allows for the storage and retrieval of persistent memories.

concepts.title: LSTM Forget Gate
concepts.one_liner: The forget gate determines which components of the cell state to discard using a sigmoid function applied to the previous hidden state and current input.
concepts.motivation_md: In long sequences, not all historical information remains relevant. The forget gate allows the network to adaptively discard information that is no longer needed, preventing the cell state from becoming cluttered with irrelevant data.
concepts.recap_md:
- Uses a sigmoid layer to output values between 0 and 1 for each element in the cell state.
- A value of 0 means "completely forget this," while a value of 1 means "completely keep this."

slots.motivation: In long sequences, not all historical information remains relevant. The forget gate allows the network to adaptively discard information that is no longer needed, preventing the cell state from becoming cluttered with irrelevant data.

concepts.title: LSTM Input Gate
concepts.one_liner: The input gate decides which new information to store in the cell state by combining a sigmoid selection gate and a tanh candidate vector.
concepts.motivation_md: To update the long-term memory (cell state), the network must decide which parts of the new input are worth storing and create a candidate representation of that new information.
concepts.recap_md:
- The sigmoid layer $\mathbf{i}_t$ decides which values to update.
- The $\texttt{tanh}$ layer $\tilde{\mathbf{c}}_t$ creates a vector of new candidate values to be added to the state.

slots.motivation: To update the long-term memory (cell state), the network must decide which parts of the new input are worth storing and create a candidate representation of that new information.
slots.key_passage:

- The $\texttt{tanh}$ layer $\tilde{\mathbf{c}}_t$ creates a vector of new candidate values to be added to the state.

concepts.title: LSTM Cell State Update
concepts.one_liner: The cell state is updated by combining the gated previous state with the gated new candidate information.
concepts.motivation_md: This mechanism allows the LSTM to maintain a persistent internal memory that can be modified over time, enabling the learning of long-term dependencies.
concepts.recap_md:
- Pointwise multiply the old state by the forget gate to drop information.
- Add the gated candidate values to create the new cell state $\mathbf{c}_t$.

slots.motivation: This mechanism allows the LSTM to maintain a persistent internal memory that can be modified over time, enabling the learning of long-term dependencies.
slots.key_passage:

- Add the gated candidate values to create the new cell state $\mathbf{c}_t$.

concepts.title: LSTM Output Gate
concepts.one_liner: The output gate filters the updated cell state to produce the next hidden state.
concepts.motivation_md: While the cell state contains all long-term information, only specific parts of that information may be relevant for the current time step's prediction or the next layer's input.
concepts.recap_md:
- A sigmoid gate $\mathbf{o}_t$ decides which parts of the cell state to output.
- The cell state is passed through $\texttt{tanh}$ and multiplied by the gate to produce the hidden state $\mathbf{h}_t$.

slots.motivation: While the cell state contains all long-term information, only specific parts of that information may be relevant for the current time step's prediction or the next layer's input.
slots.key_passage:

- The cell state is passed through $\texttt{tanh}$ and multiplied by the gate to produce the hidden state $\mathbf{h}_t$.

concepts.title: Feedback Mechanism in Recurrent Networks
concepts.one_liner: Recurrent connections allow neural networks to change their behavior based on feedback from downstream processing within the same network.
concepts.content: Recurrent connections give neural nets the ability to maintain a persistent state representation, which can be propagated forward in time or can be updated in the face of incoming experience. The same idea has been proposed in multiple fields: in control theory it is the basic distinction between open-loop and closed-loop control. Closed-loop control allows the controller to change its behavior based on feedback from the consequences of its previous decisions; similarly, recurrent connections allow a neural net to change its behavior based on feedback, but the feedback is from downstream processing all within the same neural net. Feedback is a fundamental mechanism for making systems that are adaptive. These systems can become more competent the longer you run them.
concepts.motivation_md: Feedback is essential for creating adaptive systems that can maintain state and adjust their behavior based on the consequences of previous internal processing.
concepts.recap_md:
- Recurrent connections enable persistent state representations that update with experience.
- This mechanism functions similarly to closed-loop control in control theory.
- Internal feedback allows the network to become more competent over time.

slots.motivation: Feedback is essential for creating adaptive systems that can maintain state and adjust their behavior based on the consequences of previous internal processing.

- This mechanism functions similarly to closed-loop control in control theory.
- Internal feedback allows the network to become more competent over time.

concepts.title: Recurrent Neural Nets (RNNs)
concepts.one_liner: A neural network architecture with feedback connections designed for sequential computation and modeling sequences.
concepts.content: Recurrent Neural Nets (RNNs) are a neural net architecture for modeling sequences through sequential computation rather than parallel computation. Unlike feedforward neural net architectures, which are represented by directed acyclical computation graphs, RNNs are neural nets with feedback connections. A feedback connection defines a recurrence in the computational graph, meaning their computation graphs have cycles. This allows the outputs of one layer to send a message back to earlier in the computational pipeline. To make this well-defined, RNNs introduce the notion of a timestep, where one timestep corresponds to one functional call to each layer (or computation node) in the RNN, mapping that layer's inputs to its outputs.
concepts.motivation_md: RNNs are designed to handle sequential data where the order of inputs matters, allowing the network to maintain a state and process information over time.
concepts.recap_md: - RNNs use feedback connections to create cycles in their computation graphs.

slots.motivation: RNNs are designed to handle sequential data where the order of inputs matters, allowing the network to maintain a state and process information over time.

concepts.title: Feedforward Neural Net
concepts.one_liner: A neural network architecture represented by a directed acyclical computation graph without feedback connections.
concepts.content: Feedforward neural net architectures are models that can be represented by directed acyclical computation graphs. In these architectures, information flows in a single direction from input to output without any feedback loops or cycles.
concepts.motivation_md: Feedforward networks provide a straightforward way to map inputs to outputs for tasks where sequential dependency or memory of previous states is not required.
concepts.recap_md: - Information flows in a single direction without cycles.

concepts.title: RNN Timestep
concepts.one_liner: A single functional call to each layer in an RNN that maps inputs to outputs and defines the progression of sequential computation.
concepts.content: In Recurrent Neural Nets (RNNs), the computation graph contains cycles where outputs can send messages back to earlier stages. To make this well-defined, RNNs introduce the notion of a timestep. One timestep of running an RNN corresponds to one functional call to each layer (or computation node) in the RNN, mapping that layer's inputs to its outputs.
concepts.motivation_md: Timesteps provide a discrete structure for recurrent computations, allowing the network to update its state and process sequences of data one element at a time.
concepts.recap_md: - A timestep represents one full pass through the RNN's layers.

slots.motivation: Timesteps provide a discrete structure for recurrent computations, allowing the network to update its state and process sequences of data one element at a time.
slots.key_passage: - A timestep represents one full pass through the RNN's layers.

concepts.title: Memory Propagation in RNNs
concepts.one_liner: The process by which recurrent feedback loops in an RNN propagate information across timesteps, acting as a form of memory.
concepts.content: The recurrent feedback loops in an RNN function as a kind of memory by propagating information from timestep $t$ to timestep $t+1$. This allows the network to remember information about timestep $t$ when processing new information at timestep $t+1$. By induction, an RNN can potentially remember information over arbitrarily long time intervals. Consequently, RNNs are Turing complete, meaning they can perform any computation a computer can.
concepts.motivation_md: Memory propagation allows RNNs to solve tasks that require context from previous inputs, such as language modeling or time-series prediction.
concepts.recap_md: - Feedback loops allow information to persist from one timestep to the next.
